title: Claude Study Lets You Circle Handwritten Notes for AI Help
summary: Claude Study enables students to circle portions of handwritten notes and ask questions directly. A new interface for visual note-taking assistance.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Claude Study introduces a visual interface where students circle handwritten notes to ask Claude specific questions about selected content.
- The tool bridges physical note-taking with AI assistance, allowing targeted queries without retyping or scanning entire pages.
- Currently available as a web-based concept demonstration, showcasing potential new interaction patterns for educational AI tools.


A new interface for Claude AI enables students to circle portions of their handwritten notes and ask questions about the selected content. Claude Study, officially launched on November 5, 2026, introduces a visual interaction model that bridges physical note-taking with AI-powered assistance, allowing learners to query specific concepts without retyping or digitizing entire pages.


## How Circle-to-Query Works


The Claude Study interface allows users to draw circles around handwritten text, equations, or diagrams in their notes. Once a section is selected, students can type natural language questions about that specific content. Claude processes the circled region and provides contextual explanations, clarifications, or extended information based on what appears within the selection.


This targeted approach differs from traditional document scanning or full-page OCR workflows. Instead of processing entire note sheets, the system focuses computational resources on user-designated areas, potentially improving response accuracy and reducing processing time for specific queries.


## Educational Use Cases


The tool addresses common study scenarios where students encounter confusion about particular concepts mid-review. A physics student might circle a force diagram and ask "Why does the normal force point perpendicular here?" or a history student could select a timeline entry and request additional context about concurrent events.


Key applications include:


- Clarifying mathematical steps in problem-solving work
- Expanding abbreviated lecture notes with detailed explanations
- Connecting isolated concepts to broader theoretical frameworks
- Verifying understanding of handwritten definitions or formulas


## Technical Implementation


The web-based demonstration suggests integration of vision-capable Claude models with a drawing interface layer. When users circle content, the system likely captures that region as an image input alongside the text query, leveraging Claude's multimodal understanding to interpret handwriting and spatial layout.


The interface appears designed for tablet or stylus input, though mouse-based circling remains functional on desktop browsers. Processing happens server-side, with responses streamed back to the interface in real-time chat format.


## Release and Availability


Officially launched on November 5, 2026, Claude Study is accessible as a web-based concept demonstration. The current version functions as a proof-of-concept showcasing the circle-to-query interaction model, with potential for future integration into Claude's broader product ecosystem.


The tool represents Anthropic's exploration of domain-specific interfaces beyond general chatbot interactions, tailoring AI assistance to the workflows of specific user groups rather than offering only text-box conversations.


## What This Means


Claude Study signals a shift toward context-aware, workflow-integrated AI tools that respect existing user habits. Rather than requiring students to abandon handwritten note-taking for digital formats, the interface meets learners where they already work. This approach could influence how educational AI products balance the benefits of physical writing for memory retention with the advantages of on-demand AI tutoring. As vision models improve handwriting recognition accuracy, circle-to-query patterns may extend beyond education into fields like medical chart review, engineering markup analysis, or architectural sketch annotation.
